SONA 2023

By: Liz Fish | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
What is the State of the Nation in 2023? We take to the streets with social change activist watching SONA 2023 unfold from their point of view.

Unique Selling Point:
This year Carte Blanche is telling the story of SONA 2023 from the streets of Cape Town, through the eyes of veteran activist #Unite Behind Zachie Achmat. He is part of a wider social justice movement #Fix Eskom focused on educating people about the power crisis that is impacting their lives in profound ways.
We will document the build-up to SONA- the strategizing meetings, editing of speeches, organising on the street, and attending the Defend our Democracy rally at St Georges Cathedral on the eve of SONA.
We start on the streets of Khayelitsha with Nonqaba, also a veteran activist, talking to her about her life, what she thinks of SONA, how loadshedding is impacting her, the decline of the ANC and why for the 1st time people are marching on parliament to hold their own SONA.
We will witness the unfolding of SONA from inside and outside the City hall. 40 buses will bring people from the townships who will march through the streets and hold their own SONA outside the City Hall, and if the EFF or other political parties disrupt proceedings inside City Hall we reflect what the people on the outside have to say about it.
We will witness this particular point in history, 29 years into democracy and reflect what people think the State of the Nation is in 2023.

Script:


Music
“There will now be an opportunity for silent prayer or medication-
Laughter
Script: A slip of the tongue by the Speaker of Parliament ahead of what was expected to be another politically-charged State of the Nation address.
Meditation
Script: After all, the country's many challenges were already proving a bitter pill.
Zackie Gazebo, finalized, chairs?
Deena I am not aware of the chairs
“I hope we get chairs”
Script: It's the morning of the address. Two activists put the finishing touches to their plans for the day. As veterans of the human rights movement, Zackie Achmat and Deena Bosch have seen it all - but probably wish they wouldn't be organising protests 30 years into democracy
Zackie “I want the sound to be up and running-ok
Zackie: Today we're marching on Eskom. I have never seen so much anger in the country. The difficulty is I'm also shocked that until fairly recently as a civil society, organisations haven't come together to deal with Eskom specifically. And the reason for that really worries me because we are really failing ourselves when we don't organize, think, act
Masa: it's the morning of SONA, the calm before the storm- how are you feeling
Zackie:. It's very painful to think of our country as a state of destruction 00:00:57:15The major state institutions aren't working. We don't want them to be perfect. Yeah. We just want them to function
Script: Achmat is one of the founders of the social justice movement, Unite Behind. They're using SONA to highlight their campaign #FIX Eskom
Zackie: The only expectation I have is hopefully that our protest of a couple of thousand people will be a signal that things are going to be different from now.
Script: Brave sentiments - but it was only 3 weeks ago that they started to raise funds and mobilise people to be heard at SONA.
UPSOUND
Script: For their protest to be a success, they're relying on community organisers to spread the word
Mama calling
Stalwarts are moving through their communities doing last minute organising with Mandla Majola.
Masa: You are in touch with community members and leaders here. What is their feel about the monies that are being spent on the State of the Nation address?
Mandla: there's is huge frustration from communities that Government is spending on issues that are not necessary. The whole State of the Nation address is a circus.
For the majority of the people they know that it is promises. And those promises no one will deliver.
Masa: So would you say Is it fair to say that this is actually the state of our nation?
Mandla: Exactly, it is, and it's a very sad state of our nation.
upsound
Script: Like so many, electricity cuts are making Nonqaba Melani’s life unbearable; power surges blowing her washing machine and fridge. She simply doesn't have the money to fix them. But it's living with bucket toilets for 25 years that's breaking her down.
Upsound of taking babies to the toilets
Masa: Are you still using the bucket system
Nonqaba: (crying, nods yes)..sorry
Masa: Ahh.. askies no it’s alright
Nonqaba: Ehm.. you see this thing of using the bucket system.. started a long time ago, we moved from (inaudible).. and came here still bucket system.. so from around 1998 until now. So, if you think about it.. the children that have been born since living here, how old are they? How old are they? Born in 1998 us using the bucket system.
Upsound of toilet and bucket with kids
Links- For millions of South Africans this is the State of the Nation in 2023. Promises made this week feel hollow
Script: But amid an electricity crisis, ongoing crime, and countless other social issues, surely this SONA would see a surge in civil protest?
UPSOUND
But the empty chairs at this pre-SONA rally suggest not. Among the audience, veteran activist and politician, Reverend Frank Chikane.
Frank Chikane “I get depressed because I know those politicians don't care much about the noise you make. It's when you are organized that makes a difference… The United Democratic Front could make a call and the whole country takes a stand. And that's what we require now.
Masa “ Did we think that we'd find ourselves here today in 2023?
Frank: “No. even ten years ago, we wouldn't have imagined it wouldn't be where we are. But as you know, something went wrong. 2007. It's a historical moment, . ….people with criminal intent crept in into the system and began to run the country.
Upsound of women singing at #Unite Behind office making food
SCRIPT "Back at the Unite Behind offices, there are echoes of the past... including a last minute crisis meeting to deal with a police order
Upsound from rally
They've been denied permission to march, so they've moved to plan B: a rally on the edge of the city instead of a protest in the faces of the MP’s and the president
Singing
Zackie “ I wish we could say that we are going to fix eskom now, but the truth is, that it is so broken that it is so destroyed, today we don’t have a state of the nation - we have a state of destruction
Upsound of the band
Script: And down the road, as the 8 million rand red carpet parade unfolded- no one could hear them
Upsound of the band
SCRIPT: The glitz and glam of the politicians and their guests as they paraded down the carpet - was a surreal contrast, to where we had spent the day.
Upsound of EFF
Script: The address was preceded by the now customary interjections of the opposition.
UPsound EFF
Script: But no one anticipated the EFF would take it to the next level, by storming the President on the podium
UPSOUND
Script: They got booted out the back door this time, while the media were corralled in the front
Upsound
Script: This time the President stepped immediately into the breech taking on the depressing state of the nation- head on
Ramaphosa “The people of South Africa want action, they want solutions and they want government to work for them.
Script: Announcing a state of disaster, and a ministry of electricity whose entire focus is resolving the crisis- it evoked very mixed reactions.
The President dealt with the glaring issues- Unemployment, social grants, and the rising cost of living…
Ramaphosa “ It is the job of the state to provide a minimum level of protection below which no South African should fall
Script: And then the overwhelming crime and corruption
Ramaphosa” Violent crime takes a heavy toll on every South African. ……
Script: An evening of promises, but people remain unconvinced
Frank:. It's a deep crisis, once you've got the wrong people at all levels, you are bound to produce the outcome that we are producing
Script: Another year, .. another SONA.
